result.summary: I added `GithubImporter._import_inline_images(markdown, obj, repository_full_name, created_date)` in `taiga/importers/github/importer.py`. For each distinct GitHub image URL it renders `![image]()` with `render_markdown` and takes the `src` of the first `` (the signed URL). It downloads the file with `download` and rejects it if the Content-Type is not `image/*`. The file name is the base name from Content-Disposition, or `github-attachment-` if there is none. It creates the `Attachment` as specified, saves the file with `attached_file.save`, and replaces the GitHub URL with `#`. If one image fails, it keeps the original link, calls `logger.warning` and goes on with the next image. The method is called when importing as user stories and as issues, after the object is created. The description is saved through the existing `.update()` only if it changed, and before `take_snapshot`, so the history also has the new description. I added 7 tests (11 cases). Full suite: 1702 passed, 51 failed. All 51 failures are in tests/integration/test_hooks_{bitbucket,github,gitlab,gogs}.py, and the same 51 fail on a clean checkout of HEAD, so this change did not cause them. Nothing was committed or pushed.

changes.summary: Added module `logger`, imports of `Attachment` and `ContentType` and the attachments services, and helpers: first src parser, header lookup that ignores case, safe base file name from Content-Disposition. Added `_import_inline_images` and `_import_inline_image`. Called them in `_import_user_stories_data` and `_import_issues_data` and save the description only if it changed.

New tests: attachments created and URLs rewritten (each URL imported once, base name from Content-Disposition, fallback name with extension, refresh fragment, owner/project/created_date). Failed images keep their link and log a warning (download error, non-image type, missing type, no in rendered HTML). End-to-end user story and issue import rewrites descriptions and keeps failed links.

acceptance.criterion: Imported user stories and issues point to local copies of their GitHub images, and a failed image keeps its link
acceptance.evidence: test_import_data_rewrites_inline_images_in_description[user_stories|issues] runs the real import loops: the description gets `<attachment url>#_taiga-refresh=<type>:<id>` and the failed image keeps its github.com URL. The failure paths and the logger.warning call are covered by test_import_inline_images_keeps_link_of_failed_image (3 cases) and test_import_inline_images_keeps_link_when_rendered_html_has_no_image.
